headline: CHINA EXTENDS RARE EARTH EXPORT WAIVERS 2 MONTHS — USAR SURGES 7%, ANTIMONY STOCKS +19%
snippet: China announced a two-month extension of its rare earth export-control waivers on November 9, one day before they were set to expire — triggering a sector-wide rally with USA Rare Earth (USAR) surging 7% to $8.84 and United States Antimony climbing 19% ahead of earnings. The extension temporarily relieves Western supply disruption fears while keeping pressure on US and Australian rare earth developers to accelerate domestic separation capacity; USAR separately reports Q3 results after the November 9 close, with analysts expecting losses to narrow 48% year-over-year.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES 1.25% TO $6.30/LB — RECOVERING FROM 2.5-MONTH LOWS AFTER AI ROUT
snippet: LME copper recovered to approximately $6.30 per pound (+1.25%) on Monday November 9, bouncing from 2.5-month lows near $6.24/lb hit during last week's tech-sector-driven selloff — copper's worst weekly performance since March 2026. Physical tightness signals remain constructive despite the paper-market retreat: LME-Shanghai backwardation indicates genuine immediate demand, Teck's Highland Valley Copper in British Columbia remains struck by USW workers, and Codelco faces ongoing output reliability questions that underpin the fundamental supply thesis even as macro sentiment recovers.

headline: RIO TINTO + BHP APPROVE $144M FOR RESOLUTION COPPER — FEASIBILITY ADVANCES DESPITE APACHE OPPOSITION
snippet: Rio Tinto (55%) and BHP (45%) approved a $144 million investment on November 6 to advance Arizona's Resolution Copper project — funding feasibility studies, final shaft-level material handling design engineering, long-lead equipment procurement, and water treatment facilities, building on the March 2026 land exchange that cleared the regulatory path. Resolution is targeting mid-2030s production at a deposit that could become one of North America's largest copper mines, though San Carlos Apache cultural and legal challenges remain active; the approval signals that the majors view current copper prices as sufficient justification for major long-lead capital deployment.

headline: UEC LOCKS IN 1.1M LB UNHEDGED URANIUM DEAL WITH TWO US NUCLEAR UTILITIES
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE: UEC) announced November 5 that it has signed definitive long-term supply contracts with two undisclosed US nuclear utilities for approximately 1.1 million pounds of U3O8 — 100,000 lbs per year — delivered at prevailing spot prices (fully unhedged) over six years starting 2027. The unhedged structure reflects UEC's confidence that uranium spot will continue appreciating from current levels; the company cited a peer-leading average realized price of $93.13/lb in fiscal 2026 and confirmed deliveries will be sourced from its Texas and Wyoming ISR operations, adding contracted revenue visibility while preserving full price upside.

headline: LOTUS RESOURCES INAUGURAL URANIUM SHIPMENT DEPARTS MALAWI — 145K LBS BOUND FOR FRANCE
snippet: ASX-listed Lotus Resources (LOT) confirmed its inaugural uranium ore concentrate shipment — four containers totalling approximately 145,000 lbs U3O8 — departed its Kayelekera mine in Malawi on November 2, bound for Namibia's Port of Walvis Bay and onward to Orano's conversion facility in France. The milestone marks the transition from restart to revenue-generating operation nearly three years after Kayelekera's re-commissioning began, and validates Lotus's Mercuria-backed funding structure; the company separately confirmed it is working to commercialize approximately 173,000 lbs of off-spec concentrate held from the initial production ramp-up.

headline: BUNKER HILL CLOSES SILVER47 MERGER — 'MADE IN AMERICA' SILVER CRITICAL MINERALS PRODUCER BORN
snippet: Bunker Hill Mining and Silver47 Exploration completed a court-approved merger on November 6, with former Silver47 shareholders receiving 0.1724 Bunker Hill shares per share; existing Bunker Hill holders retain approximately 57% of the combined company, to be renamed Bunker Hill Silver Corp. The merger combines the historic Bunker Hill mine in Idaho — once the largest US silver-lead-zinc mine — with Silver47's Red Mountain silver project into a domestic US critical minerals silver platform positioned to access the same government-funding programs benefiting Energy Fuels and USA Rare Earth. Silver47 is scheduled to delist from the TSX-V, Frankfurt, and OTCQX around November 9.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM FORECAST 40% — $12,000/T CALL SIGNALS SURPLUS THROUGH END-2028
snippet: Citibank cut its lithium carbonate price forecast for the next two years by as much as 40%, lowering its target to $12,000 per tonne from a prior $20,000, citing slower EV adoption growth, increased trade uncertainty, and an oversupplied market the bank expects to persist through end-2028. For TSX-V and ASX lithium developers, the downgrade removes one of the last remaining bullish sell-side anchors for near-term price recovery; lithium carbonate in China was trading near 92,500 yuan/tonne on November 9, down approximately 20% over the past month, extending a price environment that has already triggered multiple project deferrals since 2024.

headline: RICK RULE: BUY SELECTIVE URANIUM, AVOID LITHIUM — 'WRONG SIDE OF THE CYCLE' WARNING FOR JUNIOR INVESTORS
snippet: Veteran resource investor Rick Rule published a November 2026 analysis articulating a split verdict: bullish on select uranium producers and developers demonstrating resource certainty and sub-$50/lb production costs in a spot market trading near $80–$96/lb, while explicitly warning against lithium as a category he views as structurally oversupplied for the near-term cycle. Rule's key distinction is uranium's non-discretionary supply constraint — existing reactor demand cannot be switched off — versus lithium's demand-side leverage to EV policy that he considers subject to further downward revision before a sustainable floor forms.

headline: SOUTH KOREA REOPENS $14.5B US NUCLEAR PAYMENT REVIEW — NEAR-TERM URANIUM DEMAND IN FOCUS
snippet: South Korea's government is reviewing the terms of a $14.5 billion nuclear energy payment commitment tied to its planned expansion of US-designed reactor technology — an unexpected development that introduces uncertainty around the near-term demand timeline for enriched uranium and fuel fabrication services from US domestic suppliers. For uranium mining investors already navigating weak equity performance since URNM peaked, the South Korea review adds another near-term headline risk to the nuclear build-out thesis; any delay in contracted reactor capacity would reduce demand certainty even as the long-term structural case driven by AI power and decarbonization targets remains intact.

headline: MP MATERIALS AT DA DAVIDSON: COMMISSIONING PROGRESSING BUT WESTERN RARE EARTH MARKET TIMELINE UNCERTAIN
snippet: At the D.A. Davidson conference on November 9, MP Materials management outlined near-term commissioning progress at its Mountain Pass rare earth separation and magnet facilities while acknowledging that demand from EV and defense OEMs for non-Chinese rare earth supply has not yet translated into offtake economics that justify full-scale expansion. MP's shares sit approximately 53% below their 52-week high; the update arrives on the same day China announced a two-month extension of its rare earth export waivers — reducing near-term disruption pressure on Western buyers and reinforcing the structural challenge Western rare earth suppliers face in building a commercially viable alternative to Chinese processing.
